overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the December 7, 2010 water commission event was not a meeting because only one of three commissioners took part, so no quorum deliberated.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission failed to properly post notice for a December 7, 2010 event on the Bear Hill access road.
allegations.key_passage: because only one Commissioner participated in the December 7, 2010 event, there was no communication between or among of quorum of that public body, and therefore was no deliberation that would require posting notice of a meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged abutters were not notified of the December 7, 2010 event.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law's notice posting requirements do not require public bodies to provide notice of meetings to specific groups of individuals, such as abutters.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged there was no printed list for the assembly and no tally of attendance at the December 7, 2010 event.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, for the same reason, there was no requirement that minutes be kept or made publicly available.

allegations.summary: Complaint requested that the Commission hold a posted meeting with printed answers available for discussion.
allegations.key_passage: Although this was not a meeting for purposes of the Open Meeting Law, we note that the Commission did take steps to inform the public that the event was occurring by posting notice in a local newspaper for several weeks prior to the event.
